beats.say: This lesson shows how Doppler radar velocity data can reveal winds spreading out at the ground (divergence) and winds coming together inside a storm (convergence), and how velocity data led to the Tornadic Vortex Signature.

We'll cover where doppler velocity data comes from, divergence: winds spreading out at the ground, convergence: winds coming together inside the storm, spin signatures and tornadoes, limits of velocity data.

chapters.title: Where Doppler velocity data comes from

beats.say: The first Doppler weather radar started working in Norman, Oklahoma, in 1974. Researchers went on to show the National Weather Service that it was a crucial forecasting tool.
beats.caption: 1974: the first Doppler weather radar

visual.heading: 1974: the first Doppler weather radar
items: 1974: the first Doppler weather radar

beats.say: Today the National Weather Service runs a network of 158 of these radars. They're called NEXRAD, short for NEXt-generation RADar.
beats.caption: NEXRAD: a network of 158 radars

visual.heading: NEXRAD: a network of 158 radars
items: NEXRAD: a network of 158 radars

beats.say: Scientists at NSSL, the National Severe Storms Laboratory, built the first real-time displays of Doppler velocity data. That means wind information you could watch live.
beats.caption: NSSL built the first live velocity displays

visual.heading: NSSL built the first live velocity displays
items: NSSL built the first live velocity displays

beats.bullet: Velocity data can show diverging surface wind

chapters.title: Divergence: winds spreading out at the ground

beats.say: Welcome to this chapter. We're looking at diverging winds near the ground. Doppler radar velocity data can show areas of diverging winds at the surface. It can even show how strong those winds are. That can point to a downburst.
beats.caption: Diverging winds at the surface
beats.bullet: Radar velocity data can show diverging surfac

visual.heading: Diverging winds at the surface
items: Diverging winds at the surface

beats.say: Doppler radar can measure how wind moves toward or away from the radar. That's called velocity data. It lets radar spot areas where winds spread apart right at the surface.
beats.caption: Velocity data can see winds spreading out
beats.bullet: Velocity = toward or away from radar

visual.heading: Velocity data can see winds spreading out
items: Velocity data can see winds spreading out

beats.say: Why does that matter? When velocity data shows winds spreading out near the ground, it can point to a downburst. Downbursts are a source of damaging winds.
beats.caption: Spreading winds can mean a downburst

visual.heading: Spreading winds can mean a downburst
items: Spreading winds can mean a downburst

beats.say: Velocity data shows more than just direction. It can also show how strong those spreading winds are. That helps forecasters judge the danger.
beats.caption: It shows wind strength, too

visual.heading: It shows wind strength, too
items: It shows wind strength, too

chapters.title: Convergence: winds coming together inside the storm

beats.say: Velocity displays show winds moving toward or away from the radar. Convergence in the middle levels of a storm can show up there, and it can hint that a downburst is developing.
beats.caption: Midlevel convergence can hint at a downburst
beats.bullet: Look in the storm's middle levels

visual.heading: Midlevel convergence can hint at a downburst
items: Midlevel convergence can hint at a downburst

beats.say: Why does this matter? Forecasting when damaging winds will first start is one of the hard parts of warning people about severe storms.
beats.caption: Timing damaging winds is hard

visual.heading: Timing damaging winds is hard
items: Timing damaging winds is hard

beats.say: These early warning signs usually develop and change very quickly. To use them to see a downburst coming, forecasters need radar data that updates rapidly.
beats.caption: Precursor signatures change fast, so rapid-update radar is needed

visual.heading: Precursor signatures change fast, so rapid-update radar is needed
items: Precursor signatures change fast, so rapid-update radar is needed

beats.say: Here's a real case: a damaging downburst in central Oklahoma on June 14, 2011. Reflectivity is on the left, and velocity is on the right.
beats.caption: Real case: central Oklahoma, June 14, 2011

visual.heading: Real case: central Oklahoma, June 14, 2011
items: Real case: central Oklahoma, June 14, 2011

beats.say: Doppler radar measures how fast winds in a storm move toward or away from the radar. That is called velocity data. And it led to a big discovery.
beats.caption: Velocity: winds toward or away from radar

visual.heading: Velocity: winds toward or away from radar
items: Velocity: winds toward or away from radar

beats.say: In the 1970s, a scientist at NSSL found a pattern in velocity data linked to tornadoes. It's called the Tornadic Vortex Signature, or TVS for short.
beats.caption: 1970s: the Tornadic Vortex Signature

visual.heading: 1970s: the Tornadic Vortex Signature
items: 1970s: the Tornadic Vortex Signature

beats.say: What does it look like? Strong winds flowing one way sit right next to strong winds flowing the opposite way. This side-by-side pair is called a couplet.
beats.caption: The couplet: opposite winds side by side

visual.heading: The couplet: opposite winds side by side
items: The couplet: opposite winds side by side

beats.say: This discovery, along with others, helped lead to the NEXRAD radar network, also called the WSR-88D network.
beats.caption: The discovery helped bring NEXRAD

visual.heading: The discovery helped bring NEXRAD
items: The discovery helped bring NEXRAD

beats.say: Important: radar does not see the tornado itself. A TVS is not the actual tornado. It shows signs that a storm could produce one, or that one is likely.
beats.caption: Radar shows signs, not the tornado itself

visual.heading: Radar shows signs, not the tornado itself
items: Radar shows signs, not the tornado itself

beats.say: Newer upgraded radars, called dual-polarization or dual-pol, can do more. They can spot debris lofted by a tornado, and confirm a tornado is on the ground causing damage.
beats.caption: Dual-pol can confirm a tornado on the ground

visual.heading: Dual-pol can confirm a tornado on the ground
items: Dual-pol can confirm a tornado on the ground

beats.say: Radar's view has limits. The beam is the narrow stream of energy the radar sends out. Farther from the radar, it rides higher, because Earth curves away and the beam spreads out.
beats.caption: The beam climbs with distance

visual.heading: The beam climbs with distance
items: The beam climbs with distance

beats.say: So for a storm far from the radar, you may only see the rain and the winds high up in the storm. The low-level winds stay hidden.
beats.caption: Far away, you only see the top
beats.bullet: Distant storms: only high winds seen

visual.heading: Far away, you only see the top
items: Far away, you only see the top

beats.say: So when a storm is far from the radar, the beam only sees the parts high up in the storm. The important areas might not be sampled at all. Or the resolution, meaning the level of detail in the data, might be poor.
beats.caption: Far from the radar: key areas may be missed, or the detail may be poor
beats.bullet: Far from radar: important areas may not be sa

visual.heading: Far from the radar: key areas may be missed, or the detail may be poor
items: Far from the radar: key areas may be missed, or the detail may be poor

beats.say: Radar has other limits too. Some weather situations that lead to tornadoes are not easy for radar to detect. And on occasion, a tornado can develop more quickly than the radar can complete a scan and send its data.
beats.caption: Some tornadoes form faster than radar can scan
beats.bullet: Tornadoes can occasionally develop faster tha

visual.heading: Some tornadoes form faster than radar can scan
items: Some tornadoes form faster than radar can scan

beats.say: That's why storm spotters still matter. Radar usually gives a warning first. But eyes on the ground can confirm the threat, or show it isn't about to happen.
beats.caption: Spotters provide ground truth
beats.bullet: Spotters confirm or rule out threats

visual.heading: Spotters provide ground truth
items: Spotters provide ground truth

beats.say: Help is coming. Researchers are testing phased array radar, a newer kind of radar that scans the sky much faster than today's WSR-88D radars.
beats.caption: Phased array radar: faster scans

visual.heading: Phased array radar: faster scans
items: Phased array radar: faster scans
